sections.html: Pareiorhaphis vestigipinnis (Pereira & Reis, 1992). Size: 98 mm (3.9") SL. Type locality: creek tributary of Rio Caveiras at Painel, about 27°55'S, 50°05'W, Lajes, Santa Catarina, Brazil.

South America: rio Canoas and its tributaries in Santa Catarina, Brazil. La Plata, Uruguay, Upper Uruguay, Canoas.

IUCN Red List category: Data Deficient (last assessed 2018).
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

Pareiorhaphis species are primarily diagnosed from remaining neoplecostomines by having the canal plate firmly articulated to the preopercle, and by a series of sexually-dimorphic features of hypertrophied odontodes of adult males, giving the fish a hispid appearance.

Absence of adipose fin; cleithral width 27.3-31.7% SL; presence of normally developed dermal plates on the dorsal surface of body; nuptial males with few and delicate hypertrophied odontodes on the lateral margin of head, usually hidden by extensive soft fleshy lobes.
Revue française d'Aquariologie Herpétologie v. 18 (no. 4) [for 1991], pp 113, Figs. 2-3.
